title: Digital Omnibus: mandate for negotiations with the European Parliament (document 14756/26)

title: EU Digital Omnibus: the European Council adopts its position
key_claim: The Council text reinstates the right not to be subject to automated decision-making unless an exception applies, limits refusal of access requests to demonstrated abusive intention, and negotiations with Parliament are not expected before March 2027.
frame_summary: Reads the Council mandate as pulling back several of the Commission's GDPR changes and warns firms not to alter compliance before a final text.
verbatim_quote: These negotiations are not expected to start before March 2027.
verbatim_list: The Council text reinstates the right not to be subject to ADM unless an exception applies

title: When AI becomes your boss: The limits of algorithmic management

frame_summary: Argues that algorithmic management is outpacing EU data and workplace rules, and that the proposed GDPR changes could make workers' challenges harder.

title: The Council's Digital Omnibus Mandate: What Would It Change In the GDPR?
key_claim: The Council mandate restores Article 22 as a right and brings back its safeguards, but it remains a negotiating position and the trilogue with Parliament has not begun.
frame_summary: Argues that the Council keeps the Commission's direction but pulls back many edits, restoring Article 22 as a right while leaving a recital carve-out.
verbatim_quote: It also brings back the safeguards (human intervention, the right to contest)
verbatim_list: As of today, this is still just a negotiating position, not law and the trilogue with Parliament has yet to begin.
notes: Specialist legal blog, cites Council document 14756/26. Quote provenance: spans re-read on the live page by an independent WebFetch check on 21 Nov 2026 and matched; the runner egress proxy returns 403 on direct fetch.

title: EU governments call it simplification, but their Data Omnibus deal considerably weakens our rights
key_claim: The Council preserves Article 22's basic protection but clarifies that such decisions may be necessary for a contract even when a human could have made them, gives companies more room to reject or charge for abusive access requests, and Parliament faces more than 1,800 amendments.
frame_summary: Advocacy reading that the Council deal weakens GDPR safeguards and makes access and redress harder, urging Parliament to reverse it.
verbatim_quote: also clarifies that such decisions may be considered necessary for a contract even when a human could have made them.
verbatim_list: Companies would have more room to reject or charge for access requests considered abusive.
With more than 1,800 amendments tabled, Parliament has an opportunity to prioritise genuine simplification
